name: JAX
one_liner: Array computation and function transformation for accelerators.
what_it_is: A Python library for accelerator-oriented array computation and program transformation, designed for high-performance numerical computing and large-scale machine learning, per its own README. Its core is a system for transforming numerical functions — differentiation, vectorisation and compilation are composable transforms applied to ordinary functions.
why_it_matters: The functional model makes parallelism across many accelerators explicit rather than incidental, which is why it appears in large training runs. That same explicitness is the cost: state has to be threaded by hand, and code that assumes in-place mutation has to be rewritten rather than ported.
suitable_for: Numerical work where composable autodiff is the point
Research where a transform-based model fits the problem
not_suitable_for: Teams new to functional programming, where the rewrite cost lands before any benefit
Loading an ecosystem of pretrained weights published for another framework
Small models where compilation time exceeds the training time it saves
